champion: Cerebral Autosomal Dominant Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL)
ordered_diagnoses: Cerebral Autosomal Dominant Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL)

facts.raw_span: A 44-year-old man presented with a 2-year history of headache, dizziness, and imbalance
he had a history of hypertension
he had a history of cervical disc herniation
he underwent transcatheter closure for patent foramen ovale
his father had progressive cognitive decline and imbalance since the age of 50 years
his father died of cerebral hemorrhage at the age of 65 years
Neurological examination revealed brisk bilateral tendon reflexes
bilateral Babinski sign
T2-weighted fluid-attenuated inversion recovery showing lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities (WMH)
a lobe-dominant distribution of multiple cerebral microbleeds (CMBs) and relatively fewer CMBs in deep regions, mainly involving bilateral parieto-occipital lobes
a heterozygous mutation (c.754G>A, p.A252T) in the HTRA1 gene
2-year history of headache, dizziness, and imbalance

concepts.preferred_label: Cerebral Autosomal Dominant Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL)

rationales.F05: Family history of progressive cognitive decline and imbalance suggests a hereditary condition like CADASIL.
rationales.F06: Family history of cerebral hemorrhage could be related to CADASIL or other vascular conditions.
rationales.F09: Lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities are characteristic of CADASIL and hypertensive vasculopathy.
rationales.F10: Lobe-dominant distribution of cerebral microbleeds is more typical of CADASIL than hypertensive vasculopathy.
rationales.F11: HTRA1 gene mutation is a strong indicator of CADASIL.
